button_actions.fps-limit: turn the frame limit on or off (--fps-limit, default 72; Steam's own with Decky Loader; through oxp3-tool's helper)
button_actions.guide: Steam button (opens the Steam menu; hold it for Steam+button shortcuts)
button_actions.keyboard: Steam on-screen keyboard (native Steam Input: through oxp3-tool's helper; a second press closes it in Game Mode with Decky Loader)
button_actions.keyboard-chord: Steam on-screen keyboard through the Steam+X shortcut (no helper)
button_actions.ogui-menu: OpenGamepadUI menu (with native Steam Input this takes a screenshot instead)

home.label: home key (MCU button 0x24, decoded by InputPlumber as gamepad Keyboard)

xbox.label: Xbox key (arrives as the gamepad Guide button)

fixes.details:
InputPlumber 0.82 supports the OXP3 controller, but its stock map (id oxp9)
sends the keyboard key to QuickAccess2 and the home key to gamepad Keyboard.
In Bazzite's default Game Mode, which runs Steam behind the OpenGamepadUI
overlay, that makes the keyboard key open the OpenGamepadUI menu and the home key
do nothing; with native Steam Input (CachyOS always, Bazzite after
`ujust configure-opengamepadui disable`) they take a screenshot and open the keyboard.
This installs a replacement map with the same id in
/etc/inputplumber/capability_maps.d, written for the Game Mode input in use.
Defaults: ONEX/console -> Quick Access, keyboard key -> Steam on-screen keyboard,
home -> Steam menu, Xbox key -> Steam menu (as stock). Choose others with
--onex-key, --keyboard-key, --home and --xbox-key (guide, quick-access, keyboard,
keyboard-chord, home, fps-limit, screenshot, ogui-menu; `oxp3-tool list` ends
with what each does). --xbox-key also sets what the xbox-key helper does.
Some actions are not a button: a small helper service
(oxp3-tool-steam-actions.service) carries them out in your Steam session.
- keyboard (native Steam Input) opens and closes Steam's keyboard in Game Mode
  the way Steam+X does, in Steam's own interface over its remote debugging
  (Decky Loader turns it on), on any screen (over the game while one runs);
  Steam's Steam+X shortcut itself does nothing on some setups. In Desktop
  Mode, or without remote debugging, it sends steam://open/keyboard, which
  Game Mode only acts on while a game is in front. keyboard-chord sends
  Steam+X instead.
- home takes Game Mode to its Home screen (steam://open/library).
- fps-limit turns a frame limit of --fps-limit (default 72) on, and the next
  press turns it off. With Steam's remote debugging on (Decky Loader turns it
  on) it changes Steam's global frame limit, which Quick Access shows, using
  the nearest value Quick Access offers. Otherwise, or while the game has its
  own per-game profile, it sets gamescope's limit (values that divide 144 keep
  the panel at 144 Hz with VRR off). Steam is not told then: Quick Access keeps
  showing its own setting, Steam replaces the limit when it next sends its own,
  and off means 144 Hz again. Either way it caps games, never Steam's own
  screens: check it in a game that runs faster, with the performance overlay on.
Only the Steam button can be held for Steam+button shortcuts, and the
xbox-key helper can only tap, so keep guide on Home to keep them.
Check each key with `inputplumber device 0 test` (press q to quit; closing the
window instead leaves InputPlumber in test mode until
`sudo systemctl restart inputplumber`; with native Steam Input, then reboot, or on
Bazzite run `systemctl --user restart bazzite-native-steam-input.service`, to get the
Steam Deck controller back). A key that goes to the helper shows
nothing there; `journalctl -u oxp3-tool-steam-actions.service -f` logs its presses
(`journalctl -u oxp3-tool-xbox-key.service -f` for an Xbox key the xbox-key helper reads).
Your choice is kept when you apply again
(--defaults resets it). On Bazzite, apply again after
`ujust configure-opengamepadui` switches Game Mode input. The override replaces
the whole stock map, so it is only recommended while the stock map is the one it
was written for (InputPlumber 0.82.0 to 0.83.1).
InputPlumber is restarted when the map changes.
fixes.summary: Keyboard key opens the on-screen keyboard, Home opens Steam (InputPlumber map)
fixes.takes_effect: immediately (InputPlumber restarts when the map changes; reboot if the buttons act like an Xbox controller or do nothing)
fixes.title: Chassis buttons do what their labels say

fixes.details:
On some OXP3 units the controller reports the Xbox key (the lit logo key below
Home) only on its vendor interface, as button 0x25. InputPlumber 0.82 cannot
decode that id: it logs 'OXP HID: failed to parse B2 report ... 25 ...' and the
key does nothing. Which units do this depends on the button layout stored in the
controller (OneXConsole on Windows can change it); on others the key arrives as
the normal Xbox guide button and works without this fix.
This installs a small helper and a systemd service that read that interface
(read-only: nothing is written to the controller). On each press the helper
does what `oxp3-tool apply buttons --xbox-key` chose, read from
/etc/oxp3-tool/keys.json (the Steam button when buttons is not applied):
a button tap through InputPlumber over D-Bus, or a Steam action in your session
(keyboard, home, fps-limit). The key can only tap: holding it for Steam+button
shortcuts does not work (InputPlumber 0.82's hold-capable D-Bus call is
broken); use Home for those.
Files: /usr/local/libexec/oxp3-tool/xbox-key-helper and /etc/systemd/system/oxp3-tool-xbox-key.service.
Recommended when InputPlumber's log shows button 25 this boot (press the key
once, then run `sudo oxp3-tool status`).
fixes.summary: Helper that gives the Xbox key (vendor button 0x25) a job
fixes.title: Xbox key works (as the Steam button, or what --xbox-key chose)

fixes.details:
The OXP3 embedded controller drops the key-release scancodes of the volume
rocker, so volume keeps changing after the key is let go. This adds a udev hwdb
entry marking both keys as force-release. Trade-off: holding a volume key no
longer auto-repeats. Not for use with Handheld Daemon, which drops the forced
releases together with the presses (hhd#342). A reboot is needed to fully undo
it after revert.
fixes.summary: Force key releases for the volume rocker (EC drops them)
fixes.title: Volume rocker stops sticking

fixes.details:
The OXP3's BMI260 IMU uses ACPI ID 10EC5280, which both bmi160_i2c and (on
kernels with the OGC patch, such as Bazzite's; not CachyOS's yet) bmi270_i2c
claim. bmi160 cannot drive the chip. If the gyro is
missing (no IIO device named 'bmi260'), this keeps bmi160_i2c from loading so
bmi270 can bind. Only offered when the running kernel's bmi270_i2c knows 10EC5280.
Untested on hardware. Needs a reboot.
fixes.summary: Blacklist bmi160_i2c so the BMI260 IMU shows up for InputPlumber
fixes.title: Let bmi270 drive the gyro

fixes.details:
InputPlumber ships inputplumber-suspend.service, which pauses its virtual
controllers before sleep and restores them after resume. Neither Bazzite nor
CachyOS enables it. Try this if the controller misbehaves after waking from
sleep. Untested on the OXP3.
fixes.summary: Enable InputPlumber's own suspend/resume hook (shipped but disabled)
fixes.title: InputPlumber sleep hook

fixes.details:
On the OXP3 the firmware asks for ACPI 'simple suspend' on the SSD, and the
Acer Predator GM7 (PCI 1dee:1602) then fails to come back: the kernel logs
'Disabling device after reset failure: -19', the root file system drops out,
the screen stays black and the device will not sleep again until it is powered
off. nvme.noacpi=1 turns simple suspend off and fixed resume in community
testing on the OXP3. Recommended with the GM7, when the kernel log shows the
failure, or when the firmware uses simple suspend for the installed SSD;
--any-ssd applies it anyway. Costs a little battery while asleep. Needs a reboot.
fixes.summary: nvme.noacpi=1 so the SSD comes back from sleep (black screen, no further sleep)
fixes.title: SSD survives sleep

fixes.details:
gamescope drives the OXP3 panel (Samsung SDC 0x4301, the Legion Go 2 panel) with
BT.2020/PQ when HDR is on. On the OXP3 that leaves the panel black in Game Mode,
including after boot, session switches and resume, and the brightness slider
stops working. This installs a gamescope display profile in /etc/gamescope/scripts
that keeps the panel in its native gamma 2.2 mode (the Steam Deck OLED approach):
HDR still works through gamescope's tone mapping. It also lists the panel's
48-144 Hz refresh rates; --min-refresh=30 extends that down to 30 Hz (untested,
kept when you apply again). Only Game Mode (bazzite-deck images, CachyOS Handheld
Edition) uses it; it does not change HDR in Desktop Mode, where KDE always sends
PQ (keep HDR off there). gamescope 3.17 ships a Legion Go 2 profile that matches
this panel with PQ; this one takes priority over it.
fixes.summary: gamescope profile that keeps the OLED out of PQ/BT.2020 mode
fixes.title: No black screen from HDR

fixes.details:
Panel Replay is the eDP power-saving mode that most often breaks on Panther Lake
OLED panels. Setting xe.enable_panel_replay=0 falls back to PSR (selective update
where the panel supports it, else PSR1). On the OXP3 it kept the display working
in community testing but did not cure all tearing or the white dots that flicker
on dark scenes, and nobody has shown it fixes resume problems. Intel calls these
debug knobs; the kernel marks itself tainted when they are set. Costs some
battery. Never combined with xe.enable_psr=0 or xe.enable_psr2_sel_fetch=0: both
combinations gave a black screen on the OXP3. Needs a reboot.
fixes.summary: xe.enable_panel_replay=0 for intermittent black or garbled screens
fixes.title: Disable Panel Replay (xe)

fixes.details:
Makes the kernel use Intel's eDP HDR backlight interface, which switches the
panel into HDR decoding and sets its brightness in nits. Only offered when the
panel reports the interface and eDP 1.4b or older (read-only DPCD check, needs
root): the kernel never uses it on eDP 1.5 panels, which is what OXP3 panels have
reported so far. No report shows it fixing the Desktop Mode HDR black screen,
which also happens on other Intel OLED laptops (KDE bug 525650); on a Panther
Lake Dell XPS 14 OLED it left brightness dead. The kernel log hint suggesting
enable_dpcd_backlight=3 is not a reliable sign that it helps.
Untested on the OXP3: HDR brightness moves to the panel's AUX channel, and SDR
brightness too if the panel reports 'SDR brightness over AUX' (otherwise it stays
on the SoC's PWM output, and a slider that works today may stop working). Before
trying it, make sure you can boot without it: on Bazzite run
`ujust configure-grub show` so the boot menu can start the previous version (you
need a keyboard there); on CachyOS edit the entry in the boot loader's menu for
one boot (you need a USB keyboard there; with an enrolled Limine config checksum
Limine has no editor, so keep a CachyOS USB stick ready). Or keep SSH ready.
Test in Desktop Mode (System Settings > Display > HDR). Game Mode keeps HDR
tone-mapped while oled-profile is applied. Needs a reboot.
fixes.summary: xe.enable_dpcd_backlight=3 (not shown to fix HDR blanking; n/a on eDP 1.5 panels)
fixes.title: Force Intel's panel backlight interface

fixes.details:
Under gamescope the xe driver can log '[CRTC:...] DSB 0 poll error' every frame,
flooding the journal; some Panther Lake users also see cursor trails or flicker.
xe.enable_dsb=0 makes the driver program the display without the Display State
Buffer. Cosmetic: it does not fix suspend or resume. Taints the kernel. Needs a
reboot.
fixes.summary: xe.enable_dsb=0 to stop 'DSB poll error' log floods and cursor trails
fixes.title: Disable DSB (xe)
